craft_claim: Disclosure is regulated by privacy boundaries and role expectations and carries real risk; disclosures that violate audience expectations can trigger discomfort or status penalties rather than closeness.

supporting_evidence.location: Boundaries of Privacy, chapters 1-5 on privacy rule foundations and boundary turbulence
supporting_evidence.note: Disclosure is a dialectic managed through privacy rules; disclosed information becomes co-owned, and unmet boundary expectations produce turbulence, betrayal, and regret.

supporting_evidence.location: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes 144: 25-43, three laboratory experiments
supporting_evidence.note: Higher-status disclosers of weakness experienced a status penalty that undermined influence, because the disclosure violated role expectations.

supporting_evidence.location: Psychological Bulletin 116(3): 457-475, moderators of the disclosure-liking relation
supporting_evidence.note: The disclosure-liking relation is moderated by paradigm, disclosure type, and discloser characteristics, so the positive effect is conditional rather than universal.

scope: Addressed disclosure in workplace, institutional, public, and authority contexts.
exceptions: Equal-status peer relationships where weakness disclosure does not violate role expectations.
